decisions.title: Too busy to be tired
decisions.situation: Luca says it is time for a nap. You have been awake for ages and have only inspected half the room.

choices.label: Give your eyes a short test closure
Ask Luca to stay for a minute
Explain your position at full volume

result.title: Test extended
result.body: You wake up later. The uninspected half of the room is still there.

journal.text: I fell asleep while checking whether I needed a nap.

decisions.title: The two-headed jacket
decisions.situation: You manage to zip two jackets together. They are now one enormous jacket with four sleeves. This may be your greatest invention.

choices.label: Investigate whether a third one would fit
Leave your invention on the floor

result.title: Back to two jackets
result.body: You work out which zip goes where. Both jackets survive the experiment.

journal.text: I worked out how to separate two jackets I had zipped together.

decisions.title: Urgent correspondence
decisions.situation: You draw a letter and slide it into a cardboard box. It comes straight out of the missing bottom. The postal service is extremely fast.

choices.label: Fold a bottom for the box
Make a pile for each colour

result.title: Delivery delayed
result.body: The letter stays inside this time. You open the box to make sure it arrived.

journal.text: I repaired my cardboard postbox so letters would stay inside.

decisions.title: A very short biography
decisions.situation: Hannah passes you a homemade book called “People Who Smell Weird”. Your name is on page one. Every other page is blank.

choices.label: Ask why they made it about you
Write their name on every remaining page

result.title: Needs more characters
result.body: You write “repetitive, poorly researched” on the cover. Hannah laughs, then admits they could not think of a second chapter.

journal.text: I reviewed Hannah’s insulting homemade book as a disappointed critic.

decisions.title: An unclaimed contribution
decisions.situation: A loud fart interrupts the lesson. Hannah looks straight at you. Their face suggests a serious conflict of interest.

choices.label: Whisper that the chair needs repairing
Name your prime suspect at full volume

result.title: Lesson continues
result.body: Mia carries on. Hannah eventually stops looking at you.

journal.text: I ignored a suspicious look after a loud noise in class.

decisions.title: The handle is no longer involved
decisions.situation: You knock Luca’s favourite mug off the table. The handle leaves the rest of the mug. Nobody saw.

choices.label: Slide the evidence behind a plant

result.title: Bad news, delivered properly
result.body: Luca is disappointed about the mug and pleased you said something.

journal.text: I admitted breaking Luca’s mug.

decisions.title: Your parent knows this level
decisions.situation: You promise Luca one last round. They sit down, watch your first attempt and say, “I used to beat this blindfolded.” This is an outrageous development.

choices.label: Agree on one round each, then stop

result.title: Dignity preserved
result.body: You keep your promise and turn it off. Luca seems more pleased about that than any old high score.

journal.text: I stopped a game when I had promised Luca I would.

decisions.title: The cable is in your hand
decisions.situation: Luca announces that their charger has been missing for three days. You look down. Their charger is in your hand. There is still time to make this worse.

result.title: Found at the scene
result.body: Luca accepts the charger and your apology. Three days of mystery ends in approximately two seconds.

journal.text: I returned Luca’s charger and admitted forgetting about it.

decisions.title: At least you know your name
decisions.situation: Your practice exam is going badly. So far, you have written your name and the date. The date is wrong.

choices.label: Hunt for every easy mark first
Take the wreckage to Finn afterwards
Write an apology in the answer box

result.title: A rescue in small pieces
result.body: You collect enough answers to get moving. Even question one looks less hostile on your second visit.

journal.text: I recovered from freezing in a practice exam by answering easier questions first.

decisions.title: Against compulsory naps
decisions.situation: Finn assigns you to argue against replacing homework with compulsory naps. Hannah gets the other side and immediately pretends to fall asleep.

choices.label: Refuse to betray the nap movement

result.title: Evidence against your interests
result.body: You produce a solid argument about lost learning time. A yawn halfway through the speech complicates your position, but the work earns its marks.

journal.text: I prepared a class debate against replacing homework with naps.

decisions.title: Apparently this was cool
decisions.situation: Luca plays a song they loved at your age. There is a lengthy explanation of how nobody makes music properly anymore.

choices.label: Ask what it reminds them of

result.title: Before they were your parent
result.body: The story is better than expected. You learn something new about Luca.

journal.text: I listened to Luca’s old music and the story behind it.

decisions.title: Forwarded with absolutely no evidence
decisions.situation: A group chat is circulating an embarrassing rumour about someone your age. The source appears to be “everyone knows”.

result.title: An inconvenient question
result.body: Nobody produces evidence. The conversation changes topic with suspicious speed.

journal.text: I challenged a rumour in a group chat.

decisions.title: A beautiful baby cabbage

choices.label: Give it a terrible score for poor eye contact

result.title: A quiet, grounded child
result.body: You praise its composure and excellent leaves. The grower wipes away a tear. A rival arrives with a swaddled turnip and demands equal time.

journal.text: I praised a bonnet-wearing cabbage at a vegetable baby contest.

decisions.title: Everyone here is a winner
decisions.situation: At a motivational taster session, you are asked to name your greatest achievement. The person before you says they survived eight workplace investigations. The facilitator applauds and turns to you.

choices.label: Say you got out of bed today
Ask what the investigations were about

result.title: A standing achievement
result.body: The facilitator calls this a triumph over horizontal thinking. Everyone stands to applaud. You sit down before they can invent a course about it.

journal.text: I told a motivational group that getting out of bed was my achievement.

decisions.title: The quiet place has noises

choices.label: Let the ordinary sounds be there
Choose one steady sound to notice

result.title: Quiet enough is available

journal.text: I accepted ordinary background sounds in a quiet moment.

decisions.title: The lost hand

choices.label: Leave it upright on the bench
Ask around for anyone missing a hand

result.title: Please wave if this is yours
result.body: The receptionist holds the hand above the counter. A magician hurries over, thanks you and immediately removes its thumb. You stop watching.

journal.text: I returned a magician’s rubber hand to reception.

decisions.title: The door does not believe in you
decisions.situation: An automatic shop door refuses to open for you. It opens for a child, a trolley and a blowing receipt. You step forward. Nothing. The cashier points at the sensor and suggests waving.

choices.label: Ask the cashier to let you out

result.title: Assisted departure
result.body: The cashier walks over. The doors open immediately for them. They hold the sensor while you leave, like a bouncer escorting out a ghost.

journal.text: I had to ask a cashier to release me through an automatic door.

decisions.title: The naked gardener

choices.label: Ask about the plants, very specifically
Decide you have seen enough nature

result.title: A productive misunderstanding
result.body: You clear a whole bed. Three passers-by stop to stare before realising the torso has pockets.

journal.text: I volunteered beside a gardener in an alarming novelty apron in Berlin.

decisions.title: A minute without filling it
decisions.situation: You have a short wait with nothing to do. Before reaching for a distraction, you notice you have already checked the same screen three times.

result.title: The world supplies a few details
result.body: You notice a small sign and an interesting pattern of light. The wait becomes a moment rather than a gap to erase.

journal.text: I spent a short wait noticing what was around me.

decisions.title: Water with a personal brand

choices.label: Ask which emotions the filter removes
Debate the emotional lives of liquids

result.title: No emotional processing required
result.body: It tastes like water. The presenter watches you finish a glass with the expression of someone witnessing sabotage.

journal.text: I chose tap water at a premium-water demonstration.

decisions.title: Reply all
decisions.situation: You meant to send “Is that wig on backwards?” to one person. It lands in the whole public-meeting chat. The wig’s owner is typing.

choices.label: Claim you meant your own wig
Keep reopening the chat in horror

result.title: An honest public disaster
result.body: You admit it was rude. The owner replies, “It is on correctly.” Nobody asks which part you meant to apologise for.

journal.text: I apologised after sending a rude wig comment to a group chat.

decisions.title: Not the tabletop version

choices.label: Deflate it before it reaches the doorway
Climb in and ask for paddles

result.title: A long public fart
result.body: You open the valve. The canoe collapses over eight uninterrupted seconds of rude noise. The instructor waits until everyone has stopped laughing to explain the warning.

journal.text: I deflated a full-size canoe during a crowded craft workshop.

decisions.title: Inner peace is on hold

result.title: A guided loss of temper

journal.text: I relaxed through my relaxation instructor’s furious printer call.
